rationale:
Split into two leaves. Besides the accepted sibling lpf_raf_chart_change_of_variables (ccv), already a declared dependency of this node, the supplied proof contains two self-contained, reusable obligations.
(i) Step 2: the Gram Jacobian JΦ(w) = √det(⟨DΦ(w)e_i, DΦ(w)e_j⟩) of an arbitrary map ℝⁿ → ℝ^P is Borel measurable. The DAG only has the C¹ continuity lemma lpf_wtc_cat_gram_jacobian_continuous, which does not apply because Φ is only Lipschitz on Ω.
(ii) Steps 3–6: a nonnegative weighted change of variables ∫⁻ g dν = ∫⁻ (g∘Φ)·ofReal(J) dμ upgrades to Bochner integrals of Banach-valued ν-integrable F. This is stated abstractly: any measurable spaces, Φ and J a.e.-measurable, J ≥ 0, and no σ-finiteness, using the null-measurable withDensity lemmas. Stating it abstractly separates the withDensity/map bookkeeping from the heavy μHE[n]/Eucl/fderiv types.
Neither result is in Mathlib (the only map_withDensity theorem is the equidimensional map_withDensity_abs_det_fderiv_eq_addHaar) or in the DAG (all 622 nodes scanned). The same 'Bochner version from the lintegral version' step recurs in this DAG (lpf_wtc_caf_signed_of_lintegral, lpf_pi_signed_fibre_sum, slicing_im_si_signed_coarea), so the abstract form is reusable.

Parent proof after the split (assembly of the children and ccv):
(P1) ccv with g = 0 gives the first conjunct: D = Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(A) is Lⁿ-null-measurable.
(P2) Φ is Lipschitz, hence continuous, on Ω, and Ω is open, hence measurable. So Φ is a.e.-measurable for Lⁿ⌞Ω (ContinuousOn.aemeasurable), and since D ⊆ Ω also for Lⁿ⌞D (Measure.restrict_mono).
(P3) jacobian_measurable makes JΦ measurable, hence Lⁿ⌞D-a.e. measurable. JΦ ≥ 0 by Real.sqrt_nonneg.
(P4) For every measurable g ≥ 0, the third conjunct of ccv (g measurable implies a.e.-measurable) is literally ∫⁻ g d(Hⁿ⌞A) = ∫⁻ g(Φ w)·ofReal(JΦ w) d(Lⁿ⌞D)(w).
(P5) Apply weighted_transfer with X = ℝⁿ, Y = ℝ^P, μ = Lⁿ⌞D, ν = Hⁿ⌞A, J = JΦ and F. Here IntegrableOn F A Hⁿ is by definition Integrable F (Hⁿ⌞A). It yields IntegrableOn (w ↦ JΦ(w)•F(Φ(w))) D Lⁿ and ∫_A F dHⁿ = ∫_D JΦ•(F∘Φ) dLⁿ, which are the second and third conjuncts.

subproblems.title: Bochner change of variables through a Jacobian-weighted pushforward, from its nonnegative lintegral form
subproblems.statement: Let X and Y be measurable spaces (types with σ-algebras), E a real Banach space, μ a measure on X and ν a measure on Y. Let Φ : X → Y be μ-a.e. measurable and J : X → ℝ μ-a.e. measurable with J(x) ≥ 0 for every x ∈ X. Assume that for every measurable g : Y → [0, ∞], ∫⁻ g dν = ∫⁻ g(Φ(x))·ofReal(J(x)) dμ(x). Then for every ν-integrable F : Y → E, the function x ↦ J(x)·F(Φ(x)) is μ-integrable and ∫ F dν = ∫ J(x)·F(Φ(x)) dμ(x). No σ-finiteness of μ or ν is assumed.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (X Y E : Type) [MeasurableSpace X] [MeasurableSpace Y] [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E] (μ : Measure X) (ν : Measure Y) (Φ : X → Y) (J : X → ℝ) (F : Y → E), AEMeasurable Φ μ → AEMeasurable J μ → (∀ x, 0 ≤ J x) → (∀ g : Y → ℝ≥0∞, Measurable g → ∫⁻ y, g y ∂ν = ∫⁻ x, g (Φ x) * ENNReal.ofReal (J x) ∂μ) → Integrable F ν → Integrable (fun x => J x • F (Φ x)) μ ∧ ∫ y, F y ∂ν = ∫ x, J x • F (Φ x) ∂μ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3–6 of the parent proof of chart_integral_eq, with the chart data abstracted: μ plays Lⁿ⌞D, ν plays Hⁿ⌞A, J plays JΦ, and the hypothesis plays the nonnegative change of variables of step 1. μ need not be σ-finite because the null-measurable versions of the withDensity lemmas are used. Notation: ofReal = ENNReal.ofReal : ℝ → [0, ∞]; 1_S is the indicator function of S with value 1 on S; Φ_#ρ = Measure.map Φ ρ.
1. (The density.) Put f(x) := (J(x)).toNNReal ∈ [0, ∞). J is μ-a.e. measurable and r ↦ r.toNNReal is measurable, so f is μ-a.e. measurable (`AEMeasurable.real_toNNReal`). For every x, the coercion of f(x) into [0, ∞] equals ofReal(J(x)), which is the definition of ENNReal.ofReal. Because J(x) ≥ 0, the coercion of f(x) into ℝ equals J(x) (`Real.coe_toNNReal`).
2. (The weighted measure.) Let ρ := μ.withDensity (x ↦ (f(x) : [0, ∞])), the measure with density ofReal∘J with respect to μ. Then ρ ≪ μ (`withDensity_absolutelyContinuous`), so the μ-a.e. measurable map Φ is also ρ-a.e. measurable (`AEMeasurable.mono_ac`).
3. (Φ pushes ρ forward to ν.) Let S ⊆ Y be measurable. Since Φ is μ-a.e. measurable, Φ⁻¹(S) is μ-null-measurable (`AEMeasurable.nullMeasurableSet_preimage`). Then
(Φ_#ρ)(S) = ρ(Φ⁻¹(S)) (`Measure.map_apply_of_aemeasurable`, using that Φ is ρ-a.e. measurable by step 2)
= ∫⁻_{Φ⁻¹(S)} ofReal(J(x)) dμ(x) (`withDensity_apply₀`, Φ⁻¹(S) being μ-null-measurable)
= ∫⁻ 1_{Φ⁻¹(S)}(x)·ofReal(J(x)) dμ(x) (`lintegral_indicator₀`)
= ∫⁻ 1_S(Φ(x))·ofReal(J(x)) dμ(x) (pointwise: if Φ(x) ∈ S, then x ∈ Φ⁻¹(S) and both integrands equal ofReal(J(x)); if Φ(x) ∉ S, both integrands are 0)
= ∫⁻ 1_S dν (the hypothesis with g = 1_S, which is measurable because S is)
= ν(S) (`lintegral_indicator_one`).
Two measures on Y that agree on every measurable set are equal (`Measure.ext`), so Φ_#ρ = ν.
4. (Transfer along Φ.) Let F : Y → E be ν-integrable. By step 3, F is Φ_#ρ-integrable, and in particular Φ_#ρ-a.e. strongly measurable. Since Φ is ρ-a.e. measurable (step 2), `integrable_map_measure` shows that x ↦ F(Φ(x)) is ρ-integrable. `integral_map` together with step 3 gives ∫ F dν = ∫ F d(Φ_#ρ) = ∫ F(Φ(x)) dρ(x).
5. (Removing the density.) Since f is μ-a.e. measurable (step 1), `integrable_withDensity_iff_integrable_smul₀` turns the ρ-integrability of x ↦ F(Φ(x)) into the μ-integrability of x ↦ f(x)•F(Φ(x)). `integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul₀` gives ∫ F(Φ(x)) dρ(x) = ∫ f(x)•F(Φ(x)) dμ(x).
6. (Identification of the weight.) For every x and every v ∈ E, f(x)•v = (f(x) : ℝ)•v = J(x)•v (`NNReal.smul_def` and step 1). So the function x ↦ f(x)•F(Φ(x)) is x ↦ J(x)•F(Φ(x)). By step 5 it is μ-integrable, and by steps 4–5, ∫ F dν = ∫ F(Φ(x)) dρ(x) = ∫ J(x)•F(Φ(x)) dμ(x). ∎
proof_key_steps: f := J.toNNReal is μ-a.e. measurable; its coercion to [0, ∞] is ofReal∘J and its coercion to ℝ is J, because J ≥ 0.
ρ := μ.withDensity f satisfies ρ ≪ μ, so Φ is ρ-a.e. measurable.

Φ_#ρ = ν: for measurable S, chain map_apply_of_aemeasurable, withDensity_apply₀ (Φ⁻¹S is μ-null-measurable), lintegral_indicator₀, the pointwise identity 1_{Φ⁻¹S}·ofReal J = (1_S∘Φ)·ofReal J, the hypothesis with g = 1_S, and lintegral_indicator_one; conclude by Measure.ext.
integrable_map_measure and integral_map: F∘Φ is ρ-integrable and ∫ F dν = ∫ F∘Φ dρ.
integrable_withDensity_iff_integrable_smul₀ and integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul₀ remove the density; f(x)•v = J(x)•v by NNReal.smul_def and Real.coe_toNNReal.

subproblems.title: Borel measurability of the Gram-determinant Jacobian √det(⟨DΦ(w)e_i, DΦ(w)e_j⟩) of an arbitrary map ℝⁿ → ℝ^P
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P be an arbitrary map, with no regularity assumed. Here ℝᵏ = Eucl k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k), DΦ(w) = fderiv ℝ Φ w (which is 0 where Φ is not differentiable) and e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1. Then the function w ↦ √det(⟨DΦ(w)e_i, DΦ(w)e_j⟩)_{i,j<n} is Borel measurable on ℝⁿ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Φ : Eucl n → Eucl P), Measurable (fun w : Eucl n => Real.sqrt (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ Φ w (EuclideanSpace.single i 1)) (fderiv ℝ Φ w (EuclideanSpace.single j 1))).det)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof of chart_integral_eq. Notation: 𝓛 := (ℝⁿ →L[ℝ] ℝ^P) is the normed space of continuous linear maps. It carries its Borel σ-algebra (Mathlib instance `ContinuousLinearMap.instMeasurableSpace := borel _`). e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 for i < n.
1. (The Gram-determinant map is continuous on 𝓛.) Define G : 𝓛 → ℝ by G(L) := √det(⟨L e_i, L e_j⟩)_{i,j<n}. For a fixed vector v, evaluation L ↦ L v is a continuous linear map on 𝓛, and the inner product ℝ^P × ℝ^P → ℝ is continuous. So every entry L ↦ ⟨L e_i, L e_j⟩ is continuous, and L ↦ (⟨L e_i, L e_j⟩)_{i,j} is continuous into Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ with the product topology. The determinant is a polynomial in the entries, hence continuous (`Continuous.matrix_det`), and Real.sqrt is continuous (`Real.continuous_sqrt`). So G is continuous; Mathlib's `fun_prop` proves this continuity directly.
2. (The differential is Borel.) ℝ^P is complete and ℝⁿ carries its Borel σ-algebra, so w ↦ fderiv ℝ Φ w ∈ 𝓛 is Borel measurable for every function Φ (Mathlib `measurable_fderiv`). No differentiability hypothesis is needed: fderiv ℝ Φ w = 0 wherever Φ is not differentiable, and the set of differentiability points is Borel.
3. (Composition.) G is continuous between spaces carrying their Borel σ-algebras, hence measurable (`Continuous.measurable`). The function in the statement is w ↦ G(fderiv ℝ Φ w), a composition of measurable maps (`Measurable.comp`), so it is Borel measurable. ∎
proof_key_steps: L ↦ √det(⟨L e_i, L e_j⟩)_{i,j} is continuous on ℝⁿ →L[ℝ] ℝ^P: entries are continuous, det is a polynomial and sqrt is continuous (fun_prop).
w ↦ fderiv ℝ Φ w is Borel measurable for every Φ (measurable_fderiv, Borel instance on the space of continuous linear maps).
The Jacobian is the composition of the two, so it is measurable (Continuous.measurable.comp).
